title: Joe Morelle discusses manufacturing, history education, and social security in recent posts
text:
Joseph Morelle U.S. House of Representatives from New York's 25th district | Official U.S. House Headshot
Joseph Morelle U.S. House of Representatives from New York's 25th district | Official U.S. House Headshot
Joseph Morelle, U.S. Congressman representing New York’s 25th district since 2018, posted a series of statements on August 19, 2025, addressing local manufacturing, historical awareness, and social security.
In a tweet posted at 20:53 UTC, Morelle wrote: "For over 75 years, @GeneseeGlobal has been a trusted manufacturer for both local and international companies. I joined them today for a tour of their facility and to hear how we can best support their work in our community."
Later that evening at 21:07 UTC, Morelle commented on the importance of understanding American history with the following statement: “How bad slavery was” is exactly what someone who has never been to a museum would say.
At 22:39 UTC on the same day, he addressed concerns about retirement benefits by stating: "Social security is not a gift—it's a program we've paid into as Americans since we took our first job. This program sustains people who have done the hard work and put the time in. We cannot allow out-of-touch billionaires to rob our neighbors of their hard earned retirement."
Joseph Morelle succeeded Louise Slaughter in Congress after her passing in 2018 and has represented New York’s 25th District since then. Before serving in Congress, he was a member of the New York State Assembly from 1991 to 2018. Born in Utica, New York in 1957, Morelle resides in Irondequoit and holds a bachelor’s degree from the State University of New York at Geneseo.
